biological.citation: De Novo Mutations in Protein Kinase Genes CAMK2A and CAMK2B Cause Intellectual Disability (PMID: 29100089)
biological.summary: De novo CAMK2A variants identified in individuals with intellectual disability were shown to decrease or increase CAMK2 auto-phosphorylation at Thr286. All mutations affecting auto-phosphorylation also disrupted neuronal migration, establishing that tightly regulated CAMK2A auto-phosphorylation is essential for human neurodevelopment and brain function.

biological.citation: A homozygous loss-of-function CAMK2A mutation causes growth delay, frequent seizures and severe intellectual disability (PMID: 29784083)
biological.summary: A homozygous missense mutation p.His477Tyr in the CAMK2A association domain was found to impair self-oligomerization and holoenzyme assembly. In vivo, CAMK2A-H477Y failed to rescue neuronal defects in C. elegans lacking unc-43 (the CAMK2A ortholog), and iPSC-derived neurons from the patient displayed profound synaptic defects in vitro.

biological.citation: Adult Camk2a gene reinstatement restores the learning and plasticity deficits of Camk2a knockout mice (PMID: 36304100)
biological.summary: Using an inducible mouse model, adult re-expression of CAMK2A fully rescued spatial and conditional learning deficits as well as synaptic plasticity defects seen in Camk2a knockout mice. This demonstrates that CAMK2A does not play a critical irreversible developmental role, suggesting therapeutic potential for post-developmental intervention.

biological.citation: Association of CaMK2A and MeCP2 signaling pathways with cognitive ability in adolescents (PMID: 34607601)
biological.summary: SNVs in CaMK2A were associated with cognitive function in healthy Taiwanese adolescents, and plasma CaMK2A levels positively correlated with cognitive ability. Elevated CaMK2A increased autophosphorylation at T286 and upregulated downstream targets GluA1 and phospho-GluA1 in vivo, and MeCP2 was found to activate CaMK2A expression forming a positive feedback loop.
biological.sample_size: Cohort of senior high school students (exact n not specified)

biological.citation: circADAMTS6 via stabilizing CAMK2A is involved in smoking-induced emphysema through driving M2 macrophage polarization (PMID: 38936066)
biological.summary: In macrophages, circADAMTS6 stabilizes CAMK2A mRNA by forming a circADAMTS6/IGF2BP2/CAMK2A RNA-protein ternary complex, leading to CREB activation and M2 macrophage polarization. Downregulation of circADAMTS6 in mouse lung macrophages reversed M2 polarization and protected against cigarette smoke-induced emphysema, identifying CAMK2A as a key mediator in this non-neuronal inflammatory pathway.

biological.citation: CaMK2A/CREB pathway activation is associated with enhanced mitophagy and neuronal apoptosis in diabetic retinopathy (PMID: 40216954)
biological.summary: In a streptozotocin-induced diabetic retinopathy mouse model and high-glucose-treated retinal ganglion cells, CaMK2A/CREB pathway activation was associated with enhanced mitophagy and neuronal apoptosis. CaMK2A knockdown attenuated high-glucose-induced mitophagy, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation, while CREB activation exacerbated these effects, identifying CaMK2A as an upstream driver of mitophagy in this context.

biological.citation: MicroRNA-3200-3p targeting CAMK2A modulates the proliferation and metastasis of glioma in vitro (PMID: 35287547)
biological.summary: miR-3200-3p is downregulated in human glioma cells and directly targets CAMK2A; overexpression of CAMK2A reversed the anti-cancer effects of miR-3200-3p on glioma cell proliferation and metastasis. The mechanism involves CAMK2A regulation of the Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK pathway, implicating CAMK2A as a pro-tumorigenic factor in glioma.

biological.citation: NF2 can mediate the expression of CAMK2A in a tissue specific manner (PMID: 39738767)
biological.summary: Using KEGG analysis and CRISPR/Cas9 technology, NF2 was found to positively correlate with CAMK2A expression specifically in meningiomas and normal nervous system tissues, but not in non-nervous system tumors or tissues. This tissue-specific regulatory relationship suggests CAMK2A-related pathways mediate NF2's nervous system specificity and that targeting CAMK2A may be a therapeutic strategy for NF2-associated meningiomas.

biological.citation: Combining NGN2 Programming with Developmental Patterning Generates Human Excitatory Neurons with NMDAR-Mediated Synaptic Transmission (PMID: 29791859)
biological.summary: A CAMK2A::GFP reporter gene was used to identify the most differentiated excitatory glutamatergic neurons in NGN2-programmed human pluripotent stem cell cultures. CAMK2A expression marked well-differentiated neurons with greater functionality including NMDAR-mediated synaptic transmission, demonstrating CAMK2A as a marker of mature excitatory neuronal identity.

biological.citation: ASHG 2023 - IBD-focused eQTL analysis identifies an increased rate of IBD GWAS colocalizations and novel target genes using diseased tissue compared to normal tissue eQTL (N. Nishiyama et al.)
biological.summary: An eQTL analysis using diseased colonic tissue from IBD patients identified the first candidate target gene for the CAMK2A GWAS locus through a novel colocalization, a signal not detected using normal tissue eQTL. This suggests a potential role for CAMK2A in IBD pathogenesis detectable only in disease-relevant tissue context.
